title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision outlining its stance on AI usage and governance within the organization. This decision establishes guidelines for responsible AI development, deployment, and oversight.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy outlines the vacancies for technology specialists in AI, specifying the required skills, experience, and responsibilities for these roles. It also details the application process, evaluation criteria, and how the positions will support the organization’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office, outlining the role’s responsibilities, required qualifications, and the application process. Candidates are expected to have a strong background in AI research and policy, and the position will guide scientific strategy and oversight within the organization.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This document outlines the duties and responsibilities of AI legal officers, explaining how they will handle legal issues related to artificial intelligence systems within the organization. It also provides guidance on hiring, oversight, and compliance with applicable laws to ensure that AI legal officers operate within a clear legal and ethical framework.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The AI Office is currently recruiting policy officers to help shape and implement AI governance and regulatory compliance. Candidates will develop policies, oversee AI ethics, and ensure responsible deployment of AI systems.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a committee of experts that reviews and assesses AI technologies to inform EU AI legislation. They analyze risks and propose guidelines to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with European values.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document titled "Draft Standardisation Request" proposes a formal appeal for creating or adopting uniform guidelines and protocols. It outlines the need for consistency and clarity in AI practices, suggesting a framework to harmonize standards across relevant stakeholders.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This document is a notice inviting members of the Community of Practice to participate in a consultation on an upcoming policy. It outlines the consultation process, deadlines, and how participants can submit their feedback.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The document announces a call for people to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It invites stakeholders to participate and explains how they can get involved.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: CoP Graphic outlines the iterative drafting process used in developing the Community of Practice policy. It shows how drafts are reviewed, refined, and finalized through repeated cycles of feedback and revision.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The CoP Graphic outlines the timeline for drafting the policy, showing key stages from initial discussions to final approvals. It provides a visual overview of when each phase of the policy development took place, helping stakeholders track progress and key milestones.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document outlines a first draft of a code of practice, providing initial guidelines and standards for AI development and use. It serves as a foundational framework, setting out best practices and expectations to promote responsible AI deployment.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document lays out a set of guidelines for the responsible use of AI, aiming to promote ethical, transparent, and accountable practices. It offers recommendations for developers, users, and stakeholders to help ensure AI systems are designed, deployed, and monitored safely and fairly.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third draft of a Code of Practice, outlining guidelines and standards for responsible AI use. It aims to provide clear, actionable principles for stakeholders to follow in AI development and deployment.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft presents a proposed agreement on how parties should collaborate on the development, governance, and deployment of artificial intelligence. It seeks to establish shared principles, responsibilities, and safeguards to promote safe, ethical, and inclusive use of AI technology.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that outlines how organizations should develop, use, and share artificial intelligence responsibly. It sets clear standards for safety, fairness, transparency, and accountability, ensuring that AI technologies are aligned with societal values and human rights.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The policy lists specific artificial intelligence practices that are banned, such as those that could cause harm, spread misinformation, or violate privacy. It explains why these activities are disallowed and sets guidelines to help developers and users avoid them.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The document explains how to identify, name, and classify AI systems so that they can be managed consistently across an organization. It provides a clear framework that defines key characteristics—such as purpose, data use, and decision‑making scope—to help assess risks and ensure compliance.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies to encourage the growth of start-ups and foster innovation within the industry. It emphasizes communication initiatives, resource allocation, and partnerships to provide support and infrastructure for emerging businesses.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that helps new technology companies tap into European high‑performance computing resources. It offers funding, mentorship, and access to advanced HPC infrastructure to accelerate innovation and commercial success.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy outlines how to conduct a webinar on risk management, focusing on identifying and mitigating potential risks in AI projects. It provides clear guidance on assessing threats, planning responses, and ensuring that AI systems comply with safety and compliance standards.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This video webinar covers risk management concepts, explaining how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks in various contexts. It offers practical guidance and strategies for implementing effective risk management practices.
